highlights: HSIE Research is also available on Bloomberg ERH HDF <GO> & Thomson Reuters 17 November 2026 HSIE Results Daily HSIE Results Daily Contents Results Reviews ■ ABB India: ABB India’s (ABB) revenue/EBITDA/APAT was a beat by +2/+14.1/+9.6% vs. our estimates, supported by industrial end-markets, with growth coming from data centers, railways, metals & mining, food & beverage, and cement.
Structural themes such as grid modernization, renewable energy, digitalization, and India’s energy transition continue to underpin the order pipeline.
ABB’s Q3CY26 order inflow (OI) stood at INR 47bn (+56/+8% YoY/QoQ) and the backlog (OB) stood at INR 129bn (+36/+8% YoY/QoQ) as of Sep’26 (1.01x CY25 revenue).

The company continues to anticipate margin volatility for the next two quarters, led by a combination of rising costs, increased competitive pressure, foreign exchange volatility, and logistical disruptions.
valuation: The company has multiple tailwinds, namely, strong data centre demand, capex cycle recovery, revival in industrials/rail/construction segments and exports, including strong upcoming real estate deliveries and support for manufacturing policies.
We have cut our valuation multiple by 10% from 60x to 54x to factor in the near-term growth and margin volatility.
IML is well-insulated against tariff frictions as it has onsite manufacturing, and the only constraints to growth should be how quickly it can bring more capacities to capture the growth upside.
